newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian dollar strength restrains Q2 debt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian dollar strength restrains Q2 debt.

text.p: The appreciation of the Australian dollar, combined with stronger equity investment, restrained the rise in Australia's foreign debt in the June quarter, Australian Bureau of Statistics figures show.

Australians borrowed a net A$3.63 billion extra in the June quarter, but the exchange rate appreciation downgraded the Australian-dollar value of debt denominated in other currencies by a net A$1.55 billion.
But the market value of Australian securities rose in the quarter, increasing debt obligations to foreigners.
Meanwhile, the market value of Australian debt holdings abroad, particularly the Reserve Bank's reserve assets, fell.
The combined effect of these two valuation effects, plus a small change attributed to errors, was a boost to Australia's net debt of A$573 million, the bureau's figures showed.
Finally, then, net debt rose A$2.65 billion to A$187.80 billion.
Debt and equity together must finance the current account deficit, and the bureau's figures showed that equity carried more of the burden in the June quarter.
Foreigners invested A$2.73 billion in Australian equity between March 31 and June 30.
Deducting Australians' purchases abroad, net capital transactions increased equity liabilities by A$2.44 billion, compared with an A$819 million fall in the previous quarter.
But the value of both foreigners' existing equity in Australia and Australians' holdings in foreign countries fell in the quarter.

The Australians' oversease equity fell the most, especially because the rising currency reduced their assets in Australian-dollar terms, so the country's net equity liabilities rose by more than just the capital transactions.
The bottom line was a a A$3.42 billion rise in net equity liabilities to A$94.62 billion.
